components.name: benchmark-python
components.why: README identifies the root project as OWASP Benchmark for Python; requirements.txt is its root Python dependency manifest. There is no pyproject.toml or setup.py declaring an installable distribution, so this is a repository application component label, not a claim that a published PyPI package exists.

deployables.name: benchmark-python
deployables.why: app.py constructs a Flask app and defines the root and benchmark routes; runBenchmark.sh invokes flask --app app.py run --debug --port 8443 with an adhoc TLS certificate.

capabilities.why: helpers/db_sqlite.py imports sqlite3, connects to testfiles/benchmark-sqlite3.db, and creates/inserts benchmark tables; this is explicit SQLite use in the app support code.

edges.why: app.py dynamically imports benchmark modules; testcode/BenchmarkTest00099.py imports helpers.db_sqlite and calls get_connection() for its route.

components.why: One root Python application is identified from app.py, README, and requirements.txt. The repository does not declare an installable package/project name in standard Python packaging metadata.

deployables.why: The repository launch script starts the single Flask application from app.py; individual dynamically loaded test modules contribute routes to that same process.

interfaces.why: app.py defines HTTP routes, and dynamically imports the testcode modules so they register many more GET/POST routes. The current map interface kinds do not include a generic Flask application or HTTP route kind; the launcher port is documented in a shell command, not an exposed container port.

capabilities.why: Only direct SQLite use is labeled from helper code. requirements.txt has a broad pinned environment, including Flask and analysis/test tooling; dependency presence alone is not treated as proof of runtime capability.

edges.why: app.py dynamically imports testcode modules, and helper modules support those routes, but no exhaustive route-to-helper or dependency graph is represented.

notes: README describes this upstream as preliminary v0.1, so it is a small initial Python OWASP Benchmark release rather than a mature full-version counterpart to BenchmarkJava.
The testcode directory contains 1,230 Python files at this pinned checkout; app.py loads these modules into one Flask process.
Benchmark cases intentionally exercise vulnerable patterns. Security findings and test-case truth labels are outside the repository map scope.

provenance.revision_source: git ls-remote HEAD, then shallow checkout resolved to the same commit
provenance.label_scope: Source-only independent labels; dircue was not run and its output was not inspected.
